purpose: Represent how a bounded Lab capability becomes reusable outside its originating paper, product, or application without losing identity, provenance, claim ceiling, repair path, or enough instruction to be used lawfully.
posture: The Service Bus is a distribution interface, not a claim that every possible carrier already exists. Active public standards, methods, pilot packages, guided experiences, and sandboxes are shown separately from unoccupied API, curriculum, integration, and SDK ports.

transportContract.label: Identity
transportContract.question: What governed object is being transported?
transportContract.failure: Packaging quietly creates a second source of truth.

transportContract.label: Scope
transportContract.question: For which task, audience, and domain is this package valid?
transportContract.failure: A bounded method is presented as universal capability.

transportContract.label: Provenance
transportContract.question: Can the recipient trace the package back to its source, version, evidence, and decisions?
transportContract.failure: The reusable surface outlives the evidence that justified it.

transportContract.label: Claim Ceiling
transportContract.question: What may the recipient infer from the package now?
transportContract.failure: Public availability or polish is mistaken for stronger validation.

transportContract.label: Executable Instructions
transportContract.question: Can another person tell how to apply, inspect, or test the package?
transportContract.failure: The output is inspirational prose that cannot be operationalized.

transportContract.label: Reuse Witness
transportContract.question: What would show that meaning survived use outside the originating context?
transportContract.failure: Adoption is counted without checking semantic or practical fidelity.

transportContract.label: Repair Path
transportContract.question: How are defects, corrections, supersession, and dependency changes propagated?
transportContract.failure: A distributed copy becomes detached from correction.

transportContract.label: Legible Equivalent
transportContract.question: Does essential meaning survive the interface used to deliver it?
transportContract.failure: A visual or interactive carrier becomes the only lawful way to recover state.

carriers.label: Standard
carriers.role: Publish a normative or working semantic contract plus conformance questions and reference behavior.

carriers.label: Method / Guide
carriers.role: Package a repeatable procedure, questions, artifacts, and validation posture for practitioners.

carriers.label: Audit / Pilot Packet
carriers.role: Carry a bounded professional procedure into one consequential external process with explicit deliverables and authority limits.

carriers.label: Guided Experience
carriers.role: Teach or orient through resumable task paths that preserve access to deeper governed objects.

carriers.label: Sandbox / Reference
carriers.role: Let a recipient manipulate or stress a representation without granting experimental behavior canonical authority.

carriers.label: Public Record / Evidence
carriers.role: Expose work, evidence standing, lineage, and trust information so another party can inspect what supports a claim.

packages.label: Boundary First UX
packages.input: A semantic interaction paradigm and representation method developed inside Boundary First research and product work.
packages.audience: Designers, engineers, institutions, and researchers representing complex systems.
semanticPayload: views do not own semantic truth
reuseWitness: another renderer preserves the same governed meaning
consequences and context remain traceable after navigation
candidate conformance questions expose defects rather than merely style differences
packages.feedbackPath: Sandbox evidence, defects, or reusable patterns return through review before any stronger conformance or capability claim.
packages.claimBoundary: Candidate BFUX conformance levels remain proposed, not canonical. BFUX is not a mandatory skin, component library, or proof that existing design systems are obsolete.

packages.label: Software Before Code
packages.input: A software-engineering discipline for determining the represented object, protected distinctions, lawful transitions, witnesses, and closure conditions before unsafe implementation commitments.
packages.audience: Software practitioners, technical leads, architects, AI-assisted development teams, and organizations with representation-heavy systems.
semanticPayload: determine the object before the mechanism
done is a claim; closure needs a witness
reuseWitness: a new team can bound a domain and produce the declared workbench artifacts
implementation choices follow rather than pre-empt the domain model
a domain-recognized witness can distinguish technical completion from closure
packages.feedbackPath: Comparative design studies, executable reference implementations, legacy archaeology, and external replication can narrow or strengthen the method.
packages.claimBoundary: Practice levels and future tools are proposed, not canonical. The method does not claim perfect requirements, proof of correctness, framework rejection, or big-design-up-front authority.

packages.label: Agency + Representation Audit
packages.input: A bounded authority-to-repair systems analysis for one consequential software, AI, policy, or institutional process.
packages.audience: Institutions willing to inspect one consequential process rather than request an institution-wide verdict.
semanticPayload: authority and consequence may be distributed differently
representation is not the affected person or condition
contestability must exist in the executable process
source correction is incomplete if downstream consequence remains unrepaired
reuseWitness: another reviewer can reconstruct the scoped authority and representation chain
material findings trace to artifacts, rules, behavior, accounts, or labeled inference
the audit does not silently expand beyond the declared process
packages.feedbackPath: Observed process defects and inaccessible boundaries return as method constraints, domain knowledge, and future audit design requirements.
packages.claimBoundary: This package does not supply legal advice, regulatory/compliance certification, fairness or safety certification, cybersecurity certification, or delegated institutional authority.

packages.label: Guided Introduction + Atlas Paths
packages.input: The same canonical corpus projected into sequence, radial, tree, node, pathway, atlas, work, and context-halo views for different visitor tasks.
packages.audience: New visitors, practitioners, researchers, collaborators, and readers entering the corpus at different depths.
semanticPayload: branch choice and context can survive navigation
deep records remain reachable from simplified entrances
reuseWitness: a visitor can move from laboratory to practice, method, evidence, research, and formal core without losing orientation
purpose-specific entrances bypass the software path when appropriate
the retained inner corpus remains reachable rather than replaced
packages.feedbackPath: Cold-reader comprehension, practical usefulness, evidence accuracy, accessibility behavior, and progressive-disclosure quality remain human-review obligations.
packages.claimBoundary: Structural and runtime route checks do not prove usability, claim correctness, cold-reader comprehension, or rendered accessibility sufficiency.

openPorts.label: API / SDK
openPorts.note: The Lab Machine names APIs as a possible distribution form; this projection does not infer that a supported public API currently exists.

openPorts.label: Curriculum
openPorts.note: Education work may exist elsewhere in the corpus, but no canonical Service Bus curriculum package is promoted here without a source-backed distribution contract.

openPorts.label: Integration Pattern / Adapter
openPorts.note: A conceptual mapping or partner target is not treated as a maintained integration.

openPorts.label: Standalone Reference Implementation
openPorts.note: Some demonstrations and sandboxes serve reference roles; this port remains partial until a package is explicitly promoted as a maintained standalone reference implementation.

distributionRule: A capability is not ready to travel merely because it can be copied. Distribution succeeds when another party can recover what the object is, what it means, what it may claim, how to use it, how to test it, and how to receive correction without depending on hidden Lab context.
